evidence.claim: SPS Commerce describes itself as a global supply-chain network connecting retailers, brands, distributors, manufacturers, and logistics providers through shared infrastructure for modern commerce operations.

Neogen's Food Safety segment sells diagnostic test kits and complementary products to food and feed producers and processors to preserve safety and quality and detect contamination risks.
Neogen's food-safety products address pathogens, spoilage organisms, natural toxins, allergens, ruminant by-products, hygiene, food quality, and nutritional components.

Silgan describes itself as a global sustainable packaging provider for consumer-goods products, with product lines including dispensing and specialty closures, metal containers, and custom containers.
Silgan's public materials describe its customer base as consumer-goods companies and its role as helping customers bring essential products to market in efficient packaging formats.

Seneca Foods' annual report describes canned and frozen vegetables sold under private label, company-owned or licensed brands, and contract-packing arrangements; it also references case, labeling, and storage services.

Ranpak operates paper-based protective packaging and end-of-line automation solutions for e-commerce and industrial supply chains; it is a possible adjacent packaging-infrastructure name but was excluded from the four-candidate list to keep focus tighter on private-label food, compliance, and retailer qualification.

Avery Dennison designs labeling and functional materials, RFID inlays and tags, software applications, and packaging-information offerings across industries including retail, e-commerce, logistics, and food; it was treated as a larger reference candidate but not included due to the four-name limit.

memory_update.text: SPSC is a high-relevance underfollowed candidate for the retailer-supplier compliance layer: EDI/network onboarding, trading-partner integrations, supplier scorecards, and compliance logic may be second-order private-label infrastructure.
NEOG is a food-safety consumables/testing candidate; thesis depends on whether private-label/co-manufacturing growth increases testing volumes and whether integration/margin issues are improving.

SENEA is a direct private-label/contract-packing capacity candidate with low attention, but it requires careful verification of customer concentration, crop/input exposure, and whether growth is volume-driven.

The node appears investable through four public-market sublayers: retail compliance software, food-safety testing consumables, packaging converters/closures, and direct private-label/contract-packed food manufacturing.

TreeHouse Foods historically fit the private-label manufacturing node, but external context suggests a 2025 take-private transaction; verify listing status before using it in any current US-listed universe.

node: Private-label manufacturing, specialty packaging, labeling, food safety, and retail compliance suppliers
summary: Layer 1B expands the node into four US-listed candidates tied to private-label capacity, packaging formats, food-safety consumables, and retailer/supplier compliance infrastructure. The stronger chokepoint candidates are not consumer brands but enabling suppliers: retail EDI/compliance network software, food-safety testing consumables, rigid consumer-goods packaging, and private-label/contract-packed packaged foods. Claims are intentionally early-stage; later layers should verify customer concentration, retailer exposure, pricing pass-through, capacity utilization, and whether private-label share gains are actually flowing through to revenue and margins.
